teaching.hint: Is a whole grid square always one indivisible piece of a region?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: A slash can split a cell internally, so connectivity must be represented using smaller pieces whose boundaries align with every possible slash.
solution_outline.approach: Divide each square into top, right, bottom, and left triangles. Connect triangles within a square only when no slash separates them, and connect triangles across every shared outer edge. Count connected components.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Each triangle lies wholly in one region; connections join exactly pieces sharing an unblocked boundary segment.
solution_outline.correctness: Every continuous path through the grid crosses a sequence of these unblocked contacts, and every recorded contact is traversable. Thus connected components of triangles correspond exactly to geometric regions.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(n² α(n²))` time and `O(n²)` space with union-find; a small enlarged-grid flood fill is another supported approach.
solution_outline.pitfall: Treating a slashed square as one graph vertex merges regions that the slash separates.

common_wrong_turns: Connecting triangles across a diagonal wall
source_fidelity_notes: Restated the visual slash geometry in text and retained a one-cell clarification example.
